sources.entry: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is a subset of artificial intelligence that uses generative models to produce text, images, videos, or other forms of data.

summary.name: Generative AI
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia's overview article on generative artificial intelligence, the field of AI models that produce text, images, video, audio, code and other data.

reviewing ethical and societal concerns of ai

summary.what_it_does: The page is an encyclopedia overview of generative AI, covering how generative models learn patterns from training data and produce new text, images, video, audio, and code from prompts. It traces the field's history from Markov chains and early generative planning through GANs, VAEs, the 2017 transformer paper, and the rise of ChatGPT. It lists application areas such as chatbots, text-to-image and text-to-video models, drug discovery, and mathematical discovery tools like FunSearch and AlphaEvolve. It also summarizes laws and regulation (EU AI Act, China's interim measures, US actions), copyright disputes, and concerns including hallucinations, deepfakes, and environmental impact.
notable: Covers history from Markov chains (1906) to ChatGPT and modern LLMs
Discusses running smaller generative models locally on laptops, phones and Raspberry Pi
Summarizes regulation across the EU, China, US and UNESCO and ongoing copyright litigation
caveats: Encyclopedia article, not a tool; it describes many products rather than offering one
Page content is a snapshot and includes time-sensitive claims (e.g., 2026 surveys and lawsuits)
